_comment: grant-scout source registry. 'short' is the stable per-source key used by normalize.py/merge.py (normalizers/<short>.py module name) and fetch_all.sh (crawl_<short>.sh convention plus this file's own 'crawler' field). 'automatable': yes | scrape | no. 'reachable' captures last probe (2026-06-25 unless noted per-entry). Crawlers exist for entries with crawler set; deferred entries record why.

sources.name: sam.gov
sources.method: GET single public bulk CSV extract (HTTP 303 -> presigned falextracts.s3.amazonaws.com URL; follow with -L); no pagination, no session
sources.rate_limit: none — single GET, ~235MB, refreshed daily by GSA
sources.notes: Replaces the dead $SAM_API_KEY v2-API path (key returns HTTP 401/900901 Invalid Credentials, regeneration rate-limited by SAM.gov). The public bulk extract needs no key/login and is strictly better: ~85,000 records with ~65% carrying full inline Description text vs. 13,912 records / 3.3% full text from the old authenticated crawl. Contract + assistance notices incl. SBIR/STTR set-asides. crawl_sam_web.sh (Accept: application/hal+json, no key) remains available for targeted per-notice lookups only — its Elasticsearch backend caps deep paging at 10,000 results and honors no date/type filter, so it cannot enumerate the full set.

sources.name: grants.gov
sources.method: POST Search2 paginated via startRecordNum until hitCount is exhausted (a fixed rows:1200 with no paging silently dropped ~24% of live listings — fixed 2026-09-11), then per-opp fetchOpportunity for every listed id PLUS every already-known opportunity number not in the current listing (so a record that drops out of the posted|forecasted view still gets one more status check instead of freezing forever)
sources.rate_limit: polite; detail fetch is the slow part (~75s for ~1900-2400 opportunities); always re-fetches, no skip-if-exists cache (that cache previously froze close_date forever once a record was first seen)
sources.notes: Civilian-agency assistance incl. SBIR/STTR (HHS, NSF, DOE, NASA, USDA, EPA...).

sources.name: grants.gov.extract
sources.method: daily bulk XML zip (~78MB); stream-parse, filter open + Izuma-eligible
sources.rate_limit: none — single S3 GET; refreshed ~08:40 GMT daily
sources.notes: Rate-limit-free fallback to grants.gov Search2 crawler. One zip = the WHOLE Grants.gov DB incl. all civilian SBIR/STTR (NASA/NSF/DOE/HHS...). Crawler filters to currently-OPEN opps whose EligibleApplicants admit for-profit small business (codes 22/23/25/99) or is unspecified. Covers the civilian-SBIR gap left by the dead api.www.sbir.gov.

sources.name: sbir.gov
sources.method: GET HTML scrape (listing ?page=N, 10/page, default view already filtered to Status=Open) -> per-topic /topics/<id> detail pages
sources.rate_limit: browser User-Agent required (bare curl -> 403; UA alone -> 200; Accept/Referer not required); polite sleep between listing + detail fetches; ~337 open topics -> ~337+34 GETs per run, no caching by design
sources.notes: DoD + civilian SBIR/STTR topics. The old JSON API (api.www.sbir.gov/public/api/solicitations) has been dead (HTTP 403) since 2026-06-25 and stays dead — do not revive it. Replaced 2026-09-10 with an HTML crawl of the live, unauthenticated www.sbir.gov/topics website (same 403-until-you-add-a-header shape as SAM.gov's fix, not a real outage). The listing view has no visible stable sort tiebreaker, so a single pass sometimes lands short of the reported total (observed 252/337 on one run); crawl_sbir.sh re-sweeps by unique topic id (not page position) until it matches the reported count or plateaus. Output schema matches normalizers/sbir.py's existing HTML-topic-schema expectations exactly.

sources.name: dsip
sources.method: GET search (rowStart/rowsPerPage; 10/page cap, no server filter/sort — paginate all, filter topicStatus==Open/Prerelease client-side) + GET /topics/{topicId}/details for full narrative
sources.rate_limit: browser UA + Referer; 10 rows/page hard cap → ~3300 paginated search GETs for full corpus; sleep between pages + detail fetches
sources.notes: DoD SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal — authoritative DoD topic text (Army/Navy/AF incl. AFWERX/SpaceWERX). HIGHEST Izuma fit. SITE IS UP — fully working, no maintenance (verified 2026-06-29: no banner; GET search returns 32,805 live topics; detail returns objective/description/phaseN). The entire earlier 'DSIP down' story was crawler bugs, NOT an outage: (1) used POST for search (500s without session token) — correct public call is GET; (2) used wrong detail path/id — topicId is a STRING and the working detail route is GET /topics/{topicId}/details (bare /topics/{id} and /topics/details/{id} both 500). Also handles intermittent local SERVFAIL on .mil nameservers via dig @8.8.8.8 + curl --resolve pinning. GET search caps 10/page and ignores all filters/sort, so we paginate the full corpus and filter Open client-side. 'enrich' (enrich_dsip.sh) is a required SECOND pass fetch_all.sh runs right after the crawler: it pulls the published Q&A feed + attachment PDFs per topic — without it, qa_count/qa_text never populate and DSIP topics score on the bare narrative alone.

sources.name: xtech
sources.notes: Army xTech prize competitions. WordPress REST API locked (401 DRA plugin), so HTML scrape of listing + detail pages. User-requested. 'crawler_args' forces --refresh on every fetch_all run: crawl_xtech.sh's own cache-hit path skips re-fetching (and never touches mtime) when raw/<slug>.json already exists, which is exactly why this source sat frozen on its 2026-08-12 snapshot despite fetch_all 'succeeding' daily. With only ~14 competitions the cost of a full refresh every run is trivial (~30s, polite sleeps already built in), so always-refresh trades a negligible fetch cost for honest raw-file mtimes. STATUS/DEADLINE PARSING (fixed 2026-09-11): a fresh run showing all 12 competitions as status=closed/unknown with zero open initially looked like a possible parser failure rather than genuine emptiness -- investigated and confirmed it WAS a real bug, not a genuinely-empty source: xtechsearch10's detail page reads 'Submissions are due October 19, 2026' (a future date, i.e. genuinely still open), but the old status regex only matched exact phrases like 'now open'/'currently open' (never present in real xTech copy) and the old deadline regex required the due/close keyword to sit immediately adjacent to the date, which 'are due' breaks -- so it read status=unknown, deadline=None. The same adjacency bug also silently starved close_date for most of the genuinely CLOSED competitions (deadline=None), which is the more consequential half: normalizers/xtech.py turns a null deadline into a null close_date, and NULL close_date makes the active_opportunities view treat an already-closed prize competition as perpetually open forever. Fixed by decoupling date-finding from strict phrase adjacency (find any date, then check for a due/close/deadline/end cue word within 40 chars before it) and deriving status from date-vs-today comparison when a date is found, falling back to keyword sniffing only when no parseable date exists. Verified live 2026-09-11: xtechsearch10 now correctly reads status=open deadline='October 19, 2026'; 2 more closed competitions gained a real close_date they lacked before. A few competitions still legitimately return deadline=None (e.g. xtechkinetic-reach's page says only 'June 30th' with no year at all) -- left as None rather than guessing a year.

sources.name: challenge.gov
sources.rate_limit: polite; ~12 challenge detail pages; sleep between
sources.notes: The challenge.gov PLATFORM was sunset 2026-03-30 — www.challenge.gov now serves a static 'content has moved' notice with zero listings and no API of any kind (the old /api/challenges endpoint is gone for good, confirmed live, not merely relocated). The notice page itself names the successor for public listings: usa.gov's Innovation section. Crawler scrapes https://www.usa.gov/find-active-challenge (plain server-rendered Drupal HTML, no JS/browser needed, no pagination as of writing) plus each challenge's /challenges/<slug> detail page for full metadata (sponsoring agency, start/end date, challenge type, prizes, contact, apply URL). Source identity kept as 'challenge.gov' since that is this registry's stable name for federal prize competitions. 'crawler_args' forces --refresh on every fetch_all run: crawl_challenge_gov.sh's own cache-hit path is a bare `continue` that skips the detail page (and its raw-file mtime) entirely once raw/<slug>.json exists, the same silent-staleness shape already fixed for xtech below. With only 12 active challenges the cost of a full refresh every run is trivial (~15s with its built-in 1s/page sleep), so always-refresh trades a negligible fetch cost for honest raw-file mtimes — verified live 2026-09-11: without --refresh a same-day re-run reported cached-skipped=12 refreshed=0 (zero mtimes touched); with --refresh it reports refreshed=12.

sources.name: nspires
sources.method: POST (unauthenticated, no session/cookie needed) -> whole-corpus JSON, filter client-side to Open/Due-in-30-Days/Future, then GET summary!init.do?solId=<sId> per solicitation for narrative
sources.rate_limit: ~0.6s sleep between per-solicitation detail GETs; listing itself is a single POST
sources.notes: NASA solicitations. The listing page LOOKS like a form-driven JSP with no API, but it renders via jQuery DataTables in client-side mode: the whole corpus (3,467 records, all statuses) comes back from one unauthenticated POST to solicitationsJSON.do, which is what the browser's own left-nav status-facet counts are computed from. Discovered via browser network trace 2026-09-10, then verified with a bare curl POST (no cookie jar). NASA SBIR/STTR + research also reach us via grants.gov + sbir.gov; overlap is fine, merge.py dedupes by solicitation number.

sources.name: diu
sources.method: GET SSR page; parse embedded Nuxt 2 `window.__NUXT__` devalue payload (state.aois) — no browser or JS runtime needed
sources.notes: Defense Innovation Unit Commercial Solutions Openings (CSOs) + Prize Challenge AOIs. The Nuxt 2 SPA has no documented JSON API, but its SSR HTML embeds the full page state as a `@nuxt/devalue`-style IIFE (`window.__NUXT__=(function(a,b,...){...}(args...))`) — unquoted keys, bare-identifier back-refs for deduped values, a couple of pre-return mutation statements for the one shared container. NOT valid JSON but a small deterministic grammar; parsed with a pure-stdlib recursive-descent parser (lookup/nuxt_devalue.py), no third-party package. state.aois carries the complete record per open solicitation: full problem-statement/desired-solution narrative, full eligibility text, project type, close date — no separate detail fetch needed. Verified 2026-09-10: parsed count (2) and titles match the live page's displayed total exactly.
